title: Crockpot Creamy Chicken Pasta (Justin cut)
creator: Cooking in the Midwest (Luke Brown)
summary: Viral crockpot dump dinner — creamy tomato “pink sauce” chicken pasta. Adapted for no spice, higher protein, and lower carb/cal without losing the cozy pasta vibe.
whyItFits: Easy to lean protein-heavy with pasta swaps

items: 1.5–2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast (original uses 1 lb — bump for protein)
Skip the original 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
24 oz jar lower-sugar marinara (Rao’s, Carbone, or similar)
15 oz jar light Alfredo OR DIY: 3/4 cup nonfat Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup low-fat milk + 1/3 cup Parmesan + pinch garlic powder
8–12 oz protein pasta (Barilla Protein+, chickpea, or high-fiber)
Optional: big handful fresh spinach with the mozzarella

steps: Spray the crockpot. Add chicken. Season with salt, pepper, onion powder, and Italian seasoning (no chili flakes). Add garlic.
Pour marinara and jar Alfredo over the top (if using Greek-yogurt Alfredo, use marinara only now and hold the yogurt sauce for step 5).
Cook on LOW 4–6 hours (or HIGH 3–4 hours) until chicken hits 165°F.
Remove chicken, cube or shred, return to the crock. Stir in mozzarella (and spinach if using). Keep on low/warm.
Boil pasta until just al dente; drain. Stir into the crock. If using yogurt Alfredo, whisk it in off heat or on warm only, then fold in pasta.
Top with Parmesan and parsley. Serve.
substitutions: No spice: omit red pepper flakes; Italian seasoning + garlic + onion powder carry the flavor.
Lower carb: protein/chickpea pasta, or 6–8 oz pasta + spiralized zucchini; keep full chicken amount.
Lower cal Alfredo: light jar, or Greek-yogurt + Parmesan stirred in at the end.
Lower-sugar marinara: pick a jar with no added sugar.
Extra protein: 2 lb chicken, part-skim mozzarella, protein pasta.
notes: Original reel caption: easy crockpot recipe for a busy weeknight.
Original often shows Bertolli Alfredo + Prego + cellentani — swap brands for macros.
Leftovers: reheat gently with a splash of milk or broth.
Stovetop shortcut: season and cook cubed chicken, add sauces, simmer, fold in cooked pasta + cheese.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate for ~5 servings using 1.75 lb chicken breast, 10 oz Barilla Protein+ pasta, 24 oz lower-sugar marinara, light Alfredo (or Greek-yogurt DIY), part-skim mozzarella. Assumes drained pasta and sauce distributed evenly. Not lab-tested — label as estimate.

title: Mild Chicken Teriyaki Bowls
creator: Chef's Cookbook (sample)
summary: SAMPLE — Low-sugar teriyaki chicken bowls sweetened with monk fruit / 0-sugar syrup. Mild, high-protein, Asian-inspired comfort over cauliflower rice or a small scoop of jasmine.

items: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast, cubed
1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos
2 tbsp 0-sugar simple syrup (or 1–2 tsp monk fruit extract to taste)
Optional: 1 tbsp sugar-free ketchup for body
3 cups cauliflower rice (or 1.5 cups cooked jasmine for half-and-half)

steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Sear in oil over medium-high until cooked through (165°F). Set aside.
In the same pan, whisk soy sauce, 0-sugar syrup (or monk fruit), vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger. Simmer 1–2 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry; cook until glossy and slightly thick. Taste — add more monk fruit if you want sweeter, never chili.
Return chicken to the pan and coat in sauce.
Build bowls: cauliflower rice, broccoli, edamame, teriyaki chicken. Finish with sesame and green onion.
substitutions: Sweeteners: stevia, monk fruit extract, or 0-sugar syrup — start low and adjust.
Lower carb: full cauliflower rice; skip jasmine.
Extra protein: add edamame or a soft-boiled egg.
No spice: skip chili crisp / sriracha entirely — ginger + garlic carry it.
notes: SAMPLE placeholder — invent your own ratios when you cook it.
Coconut aminos are naturally a bit sweeter and milder than soy.

nutritionPerServing.notes: SAMPLE estimate: 1.5 lb chicken, cauliflower rice base, light teriyaki with 0-sugar syrup. Not lab-tested.

title: Garlic Chicken Protein Noodles
creator: Chef's Cookbook (sample)
summary: SAMPLE — Garlicky stir-fried chicken over high-protein noodles. Mild, savory, and built for Justin’s no-spice / high-protein lane. One tried + rated sample so the dashboard has a rating point.
whyItFits: Protein noodles keep carbs in check
Tried & rated sample for dashboard charts

items: 8 oz protein spaghetti or high-protein Asian-style noodles
3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos
Splash of chicken broth if needed
2 cups baby spinach or bok choy

steps: Cook protein noodles per package until just al dente; drain and toss with a drop of oil.
Sear chicken in avocado oil until nearly done. Add garlic and green onion whites; cook 30–60 seconds until fragrant (don’t burn garlic).
Add mushrooms if using; cook until soft. Splash in soy, oyster sauce, sesame oil, pepper, and optional 0-sugar syrup.
Toss in noodles and spinach until wilted and coated. Loosen with broth if sticky.
Plate and top with green onion greens. No chili oil — keep it mild.
substitutions: Noodles: Barilla Protein+, edamame pasta, or shirataki for ultra-low carb.
Sweetener: skip or use a drop of monk fruit if the sauce tastes sharp.
Extra protein: add an egg scrambled into the pan at the end.
notes: SAMPLE — marked tried with a 4.5 rating for dashboard demo.
Justin notes (fictional sample): ‘Garlic hit hard in a good way. Next time more spinach.’

nutritionPerServing.notes: SAMPLE estimate: 1.25 lb chicken breast, 8 oz protein noodles, light soy-based sauce. Not lab-tested.
